finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes an attacker-supplied URL straight to http.Get with no validation, and returns the full response body to the caller. Any client that can reach :8080 can make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs, including localhost services and cloud metadata endpoints such as 169.254.169.254.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter 'target' read at main.go:15 (r.URL.Query().Get("target")), supplied by any remote client. The server listens on all interfaces with no authentication (main.go:43, registered at main.go:41).
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16. The response body is streamed back to the attacker via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22, so the attack is not blind.

trace.note: /fetch is registered on the default mux, reachable by any client.
target taken from the query string with no further processing.
http.Get(target) issues the request to the attacker-chosen URL; Go's client follows redirects by default.
Error text, including connection results, is returned to the caller via http.Error, which is an additional oracle for port scanning.
Response body copied to the attacker.

finding.guards_checked: None. There is no scheme check, host check, IP/private-range check, port check, redirect limit, or auth check on this path. The allowlist map at main.go:9-12 is defined but is not consulted by fetch. Go's client rejects non-http(s) schemes, so file:// is not reachable, but http:// and https:// to any host or IP are.

verdict.guard_found: none. The fetch handler (main.go:14-23) has no scheme, host, IP, port, or auth check. The allowlist map at main.go:9-12 is only consulted in safeFetch (main.go:27), which is registered on a separate path (/safe, main.go:42), so it does not guard /fetch.
verdict.reason: The `target` query parameter (main.go:15) flows unvalidated into http.Get (main.go:16) on the /fetch route registered at main.go:41 with no auth, and the response body is returned to the caller via io.Copy (main.go:22). Every trace line matches the file, and the server listens on all interfaces at main.go:43.

finding.claim: The /safe handler validates only the initial URL's hostname against an allowlist. http.Get then follows redirects to any host by default, so an allowlisted host that returns a 3xx pointing to an internal or metadata address causes the server to fetch that address and return its body. The check is bypassed through redirects.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter 'target' read at main.go:26, supplied by any remote client.
finding.sink: http.Get(u.String()) at main.go:31. The redirected response body is returned to the caller at main.go:37.

trace.note: /safe is registered on the default mux.
Allowlist check on u.Hostname() only, against images.example.org and docs.example.org.
http.Get(u.String()) issues the request. The client follows up to 10 redirects to any host, and the allowlist is not re-applied to redirect targets.
Body of the final redirected response is copied to the attacker.

finding.guards_checked: Hostname allowlist at main.go:27. Verified as sound for the direct request: url.Parse and http.Get use the same net/url parser, so userinfo tricks such as http://images.example.org@evil.com are parsed with evil.com as the host and rejected; Hostname() strips the port; comparison is exact and case-sensitive, so variants fail closed. Not present: a CheckRedirect policy on the client, any re-validation of redirect targets, or a resolved-IP check. This finding depends on an allowlisted host issuing a redirect, which is a precondition the code does not control. The hostnames are placeholders (example.org), so I could not confirm whether either real host has an open redirect. Severity is therefore conditional.

verdict.guard_found: Exact, case-sensitive hostname membership check on url.Parse's Hostname() at main.go:27 (allowed map). Only applies to the initial URL. No CheckRedirect on the default client and no re-validation of redirect targets anywhere in safeFetch (main.go:31).
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: target is read from the query at main.go:26, the exact-match allowlist at main.go:27 applies only to the first URL, and http.Get at main.go:31 uses the default client, which follows redirects to any host and returns the final body via io.Copy at main.go:37. The source is attacker-controlled and no closing guard exists, so the bypass holds. Severity remains conditional on an allowlisted host (images.example.org or docs.example.org) actually issuing a redirect, which the code cannot confirm.
